ai-crash-course:
A Crash Course In Artificial Intelligence
Your guide to understanding AI and its real-world applications

What Is AI, Really?
The Simple Definition
Artificial Intelligence, or AI, is about building machines that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence — things like recognizing patterns, making decisions, or understanding language.
Think of it as teaching computers to think and learn, rather than just following pre-written instructions.

The Evolution of AI
1. Rule-based Systems: 1950s-1980s: Computers follow explicit human-written rules
2. Machine Learning: 1990s-2000s: Systems learn patterns from data without explicit programming
3. Deep Learning: 2010s-Present: Brain-inspired networks process complex information in layers

Rule-based Systems
The Prescriptive Approach: Humans explicitly defined all the rules the system should follow. If the rule wasn't written, the computer couldn't do it.
Limited but Reliable: Think of this like a recipe the computer follows, line by line. It worked well, but only within the strict limits we set for it.
Early chess programs and expert systems used this approach — powerful within their domain, but inflexible beyond it.

Machine Learning
Instead of programming every rule, we started letting computers learn from data. This breakthrough opened up entirely new possibilities.
Supervised Learning: We give the model examples with the right answers, like showing it thousands of cat photos labeled "cat" so it learns to recognize cats.
Unsupervised Learning: We hand over unlabeled data, and the system looks for hidden patterns on its own — discovering customer segments or grouping similar items.
Reinforcement Learning: The computer interacts with an environment repeatedly, learning through trial and error to maximize success at a particular task.

Deep Learning
Brain-Inspired Computing: Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning that utilizes brain-inspired systems called Neural Networks. These networks process data in layers, with each layer learning increasingly complex features.
Classification: Sorting images, emails, or documents into categories.
Regression: Predicting numerical values like stock prices or temperatures.
Representation Learning: Understanding and organizing complex data patterns.

From Prediction to Generation
1. Early AI: Prediction. Traditional Rule-Based and Machine Learning AI focused on analyzing existing data to make predictions or following strict, predetermined rules.
2. Transformer Revolution. The introduction of Transformer Neural Networks to Deep Learning unlocked the ability to generate entirely new content.
3. Modern AI: Generation. Today's AI creates original content by combining existing data in statistically likely ways via Transformers such as Large Language Models.
Generative AI Examples: Drafting emails, creating images from descriptions, composing original music, or writing functional code.

Large Language Models (LLMs)
Large Language Models (LLMs) are a type of advanced AI trained on immense text datasets. They excel at understanding, generating, and processing human language with remarkable fluency and coherence, forming the backbone of modern generative AI applications.
01 Massive Data Collection: Sourcing petabytes of diverse text from the internet, books, and articles to create the foundational dataset.
02 Pre-training: The model learns fundamental language patterns, grammar, and world knowledge from the vast dataset through self-supervised learning.
03 Fine-tuning & Alignment: The model is further refined for specific tasks and adjusted to produce helpful, harmless, and honest outputs, often with human feedback.

Real-World Generative AI Applications
Generative AI is rapidly transforming industries by creating new content across various modalities, from text to visuals and audio.
Text Generation: Tools like ChatGPT and Jasper automate writing, summarizing, and chatbot interactions, enhancing productivity and communication.
Image Generation: Platforms such as Midjourney and DALL-E create stunning visuals from simple text prompts, revolutionizing design and art.
Video Generation: RunwayML and Synthesia enable users to produce video clips from text or existing images, and generate AI-powered avatars for presentations.
Sound Generation: ElevenLabs, AIVA, and Soundraw generate realistic speech, compose original music, and create custom sound effects for various media.

Understanding AI Options
When people talk about "AI" today, they often mean Generative AI — but that's only half the story. The real skill is knowing which tool fits the job.
Predictive AI — "What will happen?" Analyzes patterns to forecast outcomes. Often faster, more accurate, and more reliable for specific prediction tasks.
Generative AI — "What could I make?" Creates new content by learning from existing examples. Perfect for creative tasks and novel problem-solving.
Smart AI users choose the right approach based on whether they need insights about the future or tools for creation.

Data Considerations
The effectiveness of all AI systems is fundamentally determined by the data used to inform their creation.
Privacy First: Special care must be taken when data is potentially personal or sensitive. Always consider who has access and how information is protected.
Fairness Matters: AI systems can inherit biases present in their training data, leading to unfair outcomes for certain groups.
Safety Standards: Using AI well means keeping privacy, fairness, and safety front and center — not as afterthoughts, but as core design principles.

Glitch's Cosmic Survival Guide
to Prompting AI

KNOW the 7 Keys to
a Stellar Prompt
Commander Glitch, your AI is your robot co-pilot. If your commands are fuzzy,
it might drift into the asteroid belt of nonsense. If your commands are clear,
it'll stick the landing on Planet Answer. Use these 7 Keys to chart your
mission!

1. TASK - Give the AI its Mission
The Task is your main quest. It's the action you want your AI robot to execute.

✅ Strong Example

"Explain how rockets escape Earth's gravity."

❌ Weak Task
"Gravity."

Mission Tip: Start with a strong verb: explain, design, list,
summarize, imagine, create.

2. CONTEXT - Provide the Star Map
Context is like your mission coordinates. It tells the AI where, when, and why the action happens.
✅ With Context

❌ No Context

"Explain how rockets escape Earth's gravity when teaching a

The AI might aim too high (university physics) or too low

class of middle school cadets."

(baby talk).

Mission Tip: Always add the who, what, where, or why so your AI doesn't get lost in space.

3. CONSTRAINTS – Set Up Force Shields
Negatives are your guardrails. They keep the AI from flying into dangerous
black holes of off-topic stuff.
✅ Protected Mission

"Explain how rockets escape Earth's gravity for middle school cadets, but
don't use math equations."

❌ Unprotected
You might end up with equations no one asked for.

Mission Tip: Use words like: avoid, skip, don't include, leave out.

4. PERSONAS - Choose the Pilot

AI can role-play as different "crew members" for your mission. This is its persona.

Space Camp Instructor

Research Scientist

"Explain rockets as if you're a space camp instructor."

Technical expertise with clear explanations

Gaming Expert

Pirate Captain

Fun analogies and interactive approach

Adventurous storytelling style

Mission Tip: The persona shapes voice, attitude, and point of view.

Communication Channel

list, or a space comic strip?

6. TONE / STYLE - Pick the Vibe of the
Transmission
Tone = how the answer feels when it beams back to Earth.

Funny

Example: "Explain black holes in a friendly, kid-friendly style with a little humor."
Wrong tone: Too scary or too robotic can make cadets tune out.
Mission Tip: Pick 1 - 2 tones to guide the mood of the message.

7. EXAMPLES - Drop a
Probe First
Examples act like test probes — they show your AI the flight path before the
real mission begins.

Send the Probe

1

Here's a sample space joke: "Why don't astronauts get hungry
after being launched? Because they had a big blast-off."

2

Launch the Mission
Now: "Write your own astronaut joke in the same style."

Mission Tip: A sample keeps the AI from drifting into space junk
responses.

Final Transmission

Clarity is rocket fuel.
Commander, remember: With the 7 Keys in your control panel, you'll keep your AI co-pilot from hallucinating space dragons and instead
chart a safe course straight to Mission Success.

Tip: Give the AI a "mini-demo" so it copies the style you want.

Quick Prompt Checklist
Did I give a clear TASK?

Did I add enough CONTEXT?

Did I say what to AVOID?

Did I assign a PERSONA?

Did I choose an OUTPUT FORMAT?

Did I set the TONE/STYLE?

Did I include an EXAMPLE?

USE the 7 Keys correctly, for without them, your ship could drift off-course into the asteroid belt of confusion! These star-tested
tips will keep your sensors sharp through every challenge in the galaxy!
